_readme: Standalone Linguistic Pattern Catalog. Edit this file to add/change detection rules without recompiling the extension. Each entry in `patterns` is matched independently by content/pattern-matcher.js; overlapping matches are resolved by content/conflict-resolver.js using `categories[].priority` and `confidenceWeight`. Optional `neutralAlternative` (pattern-level string) and/or `neutralAlternatives` (per-trigger-word override map) are shown in the highlight tooltip as a suggested, less-loaded rewording; omit either field if no good single-word substitute exists.

LOADED_LANGUAGE.label: Loaded Language
LOADED_LANGUAGE.description: Emotionally charged wording that goes beyond neutral, descriptive reporting.

EVALUATIVE_MODIFIER.label: Evaluative Modifier
EVALUATIVE_MODIFIER.description: Adjectives or adverbs that inject the writer's own evaluation rather than a neutral description.

SPECULATIVE_CONSTRUCTION.label: Speculative Construction
SPECULATIVE_CONSTRUCTION.description: Claims attributed to vague, unnamed groups instead of a named, checkable source.

ATTRIBUTION_FRAMING.label: Attribution Framing
ATTRIBUTION_FRAMING.description: Evaluative framing of how a source's statement is characterized (the verb/adverb chosen to introduce a quote).

PRESUPPOSITION.label: Presupposition Trigger
PRESUPPOSITION.description: Wording that implies an unproven or contested claim is already settled fact.

patterns.label: Charged political labeling

posConstraints.notes: Only fires when the word modifies a person/group noun (e.g. 'radical faction'), not an unrelated noun. 'extremist(s)' moved to LL-008 - it behaves as a standalone noun label, not an adjective-before-noun word (see LL-008 notes).

patterns.explanation: This word casts the person or group in strongly negative, emotionally loaded terms rather than describing their position neutrally.

patterns.label: Dehumanizing group/actor label

posConstraints.notes: Compromise tags the singular attributive form ('a terrorist organization') as Adjective and the plural standalone form ('terrorists attacked...') as Noun - confirmed empirically. Rather than require adjacency to a following noun (LL-007's approach), this just requires the trigger itself be tagged Noun or Adjective and checks both neighboring words against contextExclusions, since these words are almost always loaded regardless of syntactic position.

patterns.explanation: This term labels a person or group in starkly negative, delegitimizing terms rather than describing their actions or stated views neutrally.

patterns.label: Delegitimizing information label

posConstraints.notes: Excludes the legitimate historical/artistic-genre sense ('propaganda poster/film') via a following-word check.

patterns.explanation: Labeling information as 'propaganda' dismisses it as illegitimate persuasion rather than describing its content or sourcing neutrally.

patterns.label: Delegitimizing government label

posConstraints.notes: Excludes the neutral lifestyle/medical sense ('exercise regime', 'diet regime') via a preceding-word check - same POS tag (Noun) in both senses, so the word itself can't disambiguate.

patterns.explanation: 'Regime' frames a government as illegitimate or authoritarian, in contrast to neutral terms like 'government' or 'administration'.

patterns.label: Reputational judgment modifier

posConstraints.notes: Reuses LL-007's adjacency-to-noun gate: 'notorious'/'infamous' tag as Adjective, 'disgraced' tags as Verb/PastTense (same lexicon quirk seen with 'radical') but all three reliably precede the person/thing noun they're judging.

patterns.explanation: This word injects the writer's own negative judgment about someone's reputation, rather than letting the reader draw that conclusion from neutrally reported facts.

patterns.label: Guilt-presupposing reporting verb

posConstraints.notes: Only fires when used as a reporting verb introducing what a named subject said (e.g. 'the senator admitted that...'), not other senses (e.g. 'admitted to the hospital').

patterns.explanation: This verb frames the statement as if wrongdoing or a hidden truth is already established, rather than neutrally reporting what the source said (e.g. 'said' or 'stated').

patterns.label: Doubt-casting reporting verb

posConstraints.notes: Same reporting-verb/clause-quote gate as PS-003, but semantically opposite: 'claimed' signals the WRITER doubts the statement, vs PS-003's trigger words which signal guilt is already established. The clause/quote gate incidentally also filters out 'claim' used as a noun ('filed a claim'), since that sense is never followed by 'that' or a quote.

patterns.explanation: Using 'claim' instead of a neutral verb like 'said' can subtly cast doubt on a source's statement without the writer explicitly saying they doubt it.

patterns.label: Unattributed collective claim

posConstraints.notes: Matches the exact multi-word phrase; no single-token POS constraint needed since the phrase itself is the anchor.

patterns.explanation: This attributes a claim to a vague, unnamed group instead of a specific, checkable source, making the claim difficult to verify.
